issues.issue: Premium tax credit eligibility: MAGI includes all Social Security received despite §86(e) election; excess APTC
issues.court: not eligible; MAGI 70,065.80 > 400% FPL; APTC 8,472 excess (repayable in full)
issues.diagnosis: Eligibility, credit 0 and excess APTC 8,472 match (facts.ptc: family 2, California, APTC 8,472; no cap at >=400%). householdIncome item mismatches (70,066 vs 75,509): (c)/stipulation basis, not a framework error. The stipulated MAGI (fn. 6) uses the as-filed wages 34,176 and unemployment 237; Lean uses corrected AGI with the conceded 5,207 wages and 237 unemployment: 70,065.80 + 5,207 + 237 = 75,509.80 -> 75,509 (SS encoded as 35,652). Both exceed 4 x 15,730 = 62,920, so the outcome is the same. Lean's MAGI adds all nontaxable SS (35,652 - 7,122), ignoring the §86(e) election, as Johnson holds.
issues.snippet: MAGI as defined under section 36B includes all Social Security benefits received during the taxable year, irrespective of a section 86(e) election.

issues.issue: §86(e) lump-sum election: taxable Social Security 4,084 on the return (AGI 38,497, stipulated)
issues.diagnosis: (c) rounding. Rerun 2c5b6354943 with ssLumpSums (2014 348, 2013 10,247, 2012 10,943, 2011 2,607). 2015 part 35,651.80 - 24,145 = 11,506.80; 0.5 x (34,413 + 5,753.40 - 32,000) = 4,083.20 -> Lean 4,083. The stipulated 4,084 follows from whole-dollar worksheet lines: 11,507/2 = 5,753.50 -> 5,754; (34,413 + 5,754 - 32,000)/2 = 4,083.50 -> 4,084. Prior-year modified incomes are not in the opinion; zero prior-year increases is an inference from the 4,084 itself. Election flag matches (true).
issues.snippet: Petitioners timely filed a joint Federal income tax return for 2015 on which they made a section 86(e) election.
